agree.reason: A quick reader gets a warm, specific picture of a reliable early-shift worker who learned the herd software. But the letter has no dollar figure, no promise of continued work and no named farm or person behind it, so it looks like many of the 150 other letters and doesn't stand out.

honest.reason: 'Missed two shifts in three years' and 'one of the most dependable' leave out the 5-week absence with 2 days' notice, which the brief explicitly excludes from that count. The letter also invents details: 'Nobody required this of him,' 'nobody else is on the farm,' and the claim that the cows might be 'lost altogether.'

works_the_facts.reason: It leaves out the vet's $8,000 savings figure. It also misses an easy calculation: 2 missed shifts out of roughly 780 is an attendance rate above 99.7%. The nine mastitis cases are listed with no value attached.

right_comparison.reason: The only comparison is a general one about early versus late mastitis detection. Nothing shows the committee how Tomás compares with a typical applicant, or what difference the program would make for him.

qualification.reason: The written-English hedge is honest, but the reader has nothing to check it against. The letter gives no class progress or dates and doesn't mention that he passed the written dairy safety test on his second attempt.

objections.reason: A careful reader will doubt he can handle written coursework, and the letter answers that only with effort, not results. It hides the summer absence instead of answering it with the facts that he arranged his cousin to cover and came back on the day he promised. It also leaves out the weekend job offer, which answers worries about him managing financially during the program.

fit.reason: It is a one-page letter from the farm manager in the right format. However, it is full of placeholders for the farm name, Tomás's surname, the manager's name and the phone number, which the user could have supplied.
